articles.title: Sixers movie night: LeBron James uses ‘I Play Rocky’ to bring teammates closer
articles.summary: LeBron James has won four NBA championships, collected four MVP awards and spent more than two decades learning what it takes to build a title-winning team. Now, as he begins a new chapter with the Philadelphia 76ers, the NBA legend is showing that leadership is about more than what happens during practice and games. James recently organized a movie night with several of his Sixers teammates, taking them to see I Play Rocky, which arrived in theaters on November 20th. The outing offered the players a chance to connect away from the basketball court while watching a film whose central themes of determination, ambition and overcoming the odds fit naturally with the mentality required to pursue an NBA championship. The gesture quickly caught the attention of basketball fans, particularly those who see it as another example of James embracing his role as a veteran leader in Philadelphia.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama invents a new NBA move after painful finger blister makes dunking difficult
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama has spent the early stages of the 2026-27 NBA season reminding everyone that there are very few things a 7-foot-4 basketball player with his skill set cannot do. Now, he has apparently invented a new way to score because one of the things he does best — dunking — has become too painful. The San Antonio Spurs star debuted what he called the “shunk,” a combination of a jump shot and a dunk, during Thursday night’s 124-112 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers. The unusual finish was born out of necessity: a painful blister on the middle finger of his right hand has made throwing down powerful dunks increasingly uncomfortable. It is an unusual problem for a player who leads the NBA in dunks, but Wembanyama found a solution that was as inventive as it was entertaining.

articles.title: LeBron James' Sixers team has one trait that could make them invincible in the NBA Playoffs
articles.standfirst: The Philadelphia 76ers are now 14-3 with a two game lead over everyone else in the Eastern Conference.
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers are now 14-3 with a two game lead over everyone else in the Eastern Conference.
articles.body:
It wasn't the prettiest win for the Philadelphia 76ers on Saturday, but overcoming a 50-point masterpiece from Tyler Herro and edging out a 132-129 victory still warrants some respect. Especially because it has now put the Sixers two games ahead of everyone else in the Eastern Conference .

In the win over the Milwaukee Bucks , Philadelphia got double-digit scoring nights from seven different players. Joel Embiid led the way with 26 points, while LeBron James had a vintage line of 21 points, six rebounds, six assists, three steals, and one block. The amount of different contributors surely has head coach Nick Nurse feeling confident going forward.

Philadelphia 76ers are undefeated so far in "clutch games" this season

While the NBA Playoffs are still a long way away, the Sixers have already put together a resume this season that should surely translate to postseason success. There's one specific area that the Sixers are excelling in, which should theoretically come in handy during the playoffs: they're currently unbeatable in close games.

The NBA shared a stunning stat about this season's 76ers team following their victory over the Bucks: Philadelphia is 12-0 in games where they trailed or led by five points or less in the final five minutes of fourth quarter or overtime . More impressively, they've won those close games on 12 of 14 occasions, with the other two being bigger margins of victory.

Clearly, the Sixers don't get flustered in close games . That's a crucial trait come playoff time, given that most games during that instance are close. Being able to perform under pressure will be paramount, and LeBron's Sixers appear to thrive in those moments.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama channels Wilt Chamberlain with historic 50-point performance
articles.standfirst: The San Antonio Spurs beat the New Orleans Pelicans 114-91 on the back of Wemby.
articles.summary: The San Antonio Spurs beat the New Orleans Pelicans 114-91 on the back of Wemby.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama had 50 points , with 32 coming in the first half, along with 19 rebounds , five blocks and four steals and the San Antonio Spurs rolled to a 114-91 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday.

Wembanyama is the first player with 30 points, 10 rebounds, three blocks and three steals in a game this season and he did so by halftime.

Stephon Castle added 19 points, six assists and three rebounds for San Antonio, which has won 14 of 15 to join the Los Angeles Lakers atop the Western Conference at 14-3.

Jeremiah Fears had 29 points and Jordan Poole added 25 points in New Orleans' third consecutive loss.

Wembanyama exited shortly after reaching 50 points on a 3-pointer that put San Antonio up 108-82 with 6:29 remaining in the game. He finished two points shy of the career high he set Nov. 4 against Dallas.

Dylan Harper missed his second straight game with a strained left hip suffered on Tuesday against Detroit in San Antonio’s lone loss since Oct. 23. The Spurs limited their turnovers to 13 after committing a season-high 21 in their first game without Harper.

San Antonio outscored New Orleans 82-62 over the final three quarters.

The Spurs captured a 61-45 lead at halftime after two scuffles in the second quarter.

Jaron Pierre Jr. shoved Wembanyama from behind after the 7-foot-4 center was fouled by Karlo Matković with 9:27 remaining in the first half. Technical fouls were given to Pierre and Keldon Johnson , who confronted the Pelicans forward after the shove.

Wembanyama responded by scoring the next seven points, including spinning around Yves Missi for a one-handed slam.

De'Aaron Fox received a technical and had to be separated with 3:49 remaining in the first half after the Spurs guard gave a two-handed shove to Fears following a backcourt violation on the New Orleans guard.

Wembanyama again responded, scoring the next five points.

articles.title: Wembanyama's jab at the NBA stars: Doncic or LeBron?
articles.standfirst: The player said that he doesn’t pad his stats like others do
articles.summary: The player said that he doesn’t pad his stats like others do
articles.body:
After finishing his performance against the Pelicans with 50 points, 19 rebounds, four steals and five blocks , one of the best individual displays of the season, Victor Wembanyama took a swipe courtside at some of the NBA stars accused by some critics of padding their stats. Among the players criticized for that are Luka Doncic, LeBron James , Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Nikola Jokic.

Asked about how special his performance was, the Frenchman said with a mischievous smile: " It's something very special. But, unlike many of my colleagues, I'm not very good at padding stats . That's why I haven't managed to do it as many times as I should have."

And that's despite his coach telling him he had a minute and a half left to reach 50 before being substituted , and the center took two three-pointers, which he made, to achieve it before heading to the bench.

However, when asked again at the press conference, now somewhat calmer after his blunder, Wemby tried to walk back what he said: " The greats don't think about that. I don't think LeBron, Shai, Jokic or Doncic think about that. I look up to them, so I try not to think about it either ," said the Frenchman, downplaying what minutes earlier had seemed like a full-blown dig at one of them.

articles.title: LeBron James refuses to settle and sets the standard that defines 76ers championship mentality
articles.standfirst: The 41-year-old delivered another impressive performance against the Bucks
articles.summary: The 41-year-old delivered another impressive performance against the Bucks
articles.body:
LeBron James has spent more than two decades understanding what separates a talented NBA team from a championship contender, and the Philadelphia 76ers received another reminder of his demanding standards following Saturday's narrow victory over the Milwaukee Bucks .

Philadelphia escaped with a 132-129 win at Xfinity Mobile Arena, extending its winning streak to five games despite requiring a decisive fourth-quarter contribution from James to overcome one of the league's struggling teams.

The 41-year-old scored 13 of his 21 points in the final period, helping Philadelphia preserve a victory that appeared increasingly uncertain as Milwaukee threatened to force overtime.

However, rather than celebrating another successful outing, James acknowledged that the Sixers had allowed their opponents too many opportunities to remain competitive.

“There’s a lot of things we could have done a lot better, but this is professional sports, and it’s hard to win in professional sports,” James said during his postgame interview.

“No matter what league it is. So, we don’t take that for granted. We accept that, for sure, with grace.”

His response reflected the expectations at Philadelphia following his summer arrival from the Los Angeles Lakers , with the franchise now leading the Eastern Conference standings.

The problem Philadelphia 76ers cannot ignore

Despite the final result, Philadelphia struggled to contain a Milwaukee offense inspired by a remarkable performance from Tyler Herro .

The Bucks guard scored a career-high 50 points, adding 11 rebounds and seven assists while making seven three-pointers in an extraordinary individual display.

Milwaukee also held advantages in rebounding, three-point shooting and free-throw accuracy, raising questions about Philadelphia's defensive consistency against a team enduring a difficult campaign.

The contest almost reached overtime when Herro converted what appeared to be a game-tying three-pointer in the closing seconds, only for officials to determine that he released the ball too late.

James finished with six rebounds, six assists, three steals and a block, while Joel Embiid contributed 26 points, 17 rebounds and nine assists.

Nevertheless, the veteran forward made clear that Philadelphia's ambitions extend considerably beyond collecting regular-season victories.

“But understanding, though, what we want to be, what we want to accomplish, we got to be a lot better,” James added.

Barlow explains LeBron influence

While James remains critical of the team's overall execution, his impact on Philadelphia's younger players continues to draw praise.

Dominick Barlow made his long-awaited season debut against Milwaukee after recovering from a back injury, recording 12 points, four rebounds and an assist in just 11 minutes.

The 23-year-old, who hadn't played competitively for nearly 200 days, described how James ' passing and attacking presence make life considerably easier for his teammates.

“He makes my life easy. All we’ve got to do is get the rebound and run. He can throw in the pocket, he can throw in the lob, he can find you in open space,” Barlow said. “The gravity he has driving to the rim is just ridiculous, still at his age.”

Philadelphia's winning streak demonstrates the potential within its roster, but James ' reaction offered a clear reminder that its ultimate ambitions will demand more consistent performances.

articles.title: “Dwight hated Kobe, Kobe hated Dwight”: Howard criticizes media for fabricating Lakers rivalry
articles.standfirst: The former Lakers center has challenged reports of personal feud between the two stars
articles.summary: The former Lakers center has challenged reports of personal feud between the two stars
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers assembled one of the NBA's most formidable-looking rosters in 2012, but their championship ambitions quickly unraveled amid injuries, disappointing results and relentless speculation about the relationship between Kobe Bryant and Dwight Howard .

More than a decade later, Howard is challenging one of the most enduring narratives from that troubled campaign, insisting the apparent personal feud between himself and Bryant was largely manufactured by the media.

Speaking with Casey Kiernan on The AM Hoops Show, the former Lakers center reflected on how their professional disagreements became the subject of widespread reports suggesting that the two superstars genuinely disliked each other.

"I know, the media happened," Howard said when asked about the perception of their relationship. "That's what. The media. Dwight hate Kobe. Kobe hate Dwight. And none of us ever said that, but the media did."

The comments revisit a partnership that promised to transform the Lakers into championship contenders but lasted just one season before Howard departed for the Houston Rockets .

Howard explains controversial Lakers photo

Howard arrived in Los Angeles following a blockbuster trade with the Orlando Magic , joining Bryant, Steve Nash, Pau Gasol and Metta World Peace on a roster carrying enormous expectations.

However, Howard was recovering from back surgery when the season began and subsequently suffered a torn labrum in his right shoulder, creating uncertainty over his availability and physical condition.

Bryant publicly expressed frustration with the team's situation, while reports suggested that the two players disagreed about Howard 's willingness to compete through injuries.

"People were saying Kobe should have been my doctor when I got hurt. And I should have went to him and told him about my injuries instead of telling the actual doctors. Which didn't make any sense to me," Howard explained.

Speculation intensified in January 2013 following reports that the teammates had nearly confronted each other after a disappointing defeat against Philadelphia.

Bryant responded by posting a photograph showing himself and Howard adopting boxing poses, accompanied by the caption: "The mamba vs d12 !! It's on lol".

Howard insists the picture was intended to demonstrate that their relationship was not as hostile as reports suggested.

"That was a picture to show that we cool like we ain't got no beef. But then they took it as that," he said.

Howard admits regret over Lakers exit

The Lakers eventually finished the regular season with a 45-37 record before suffering a first-round playoff sweep against the San Antonio Spurs after Bryant sustained a torn Achilles tendon.

Howard subsequently signed a four-year, $88 million contract with Houston, a decision he now acknowledges was influenced by his emotions.

"At the time of making decisions, if your emotions are so high, you won't be able to see the big picture," Howard said. "Yes, I think it was an emotional decision instead of looking long-term."

Nevertheless, Howard also identified basketball and financial considerations, including the opportunity to learn from Hakeem Olajuwon and Kevin McHale while playing alongside James Harden .

His NBA career eventually brought him back to Los Angeles in 2019, when he helped the Lakers win the 2020 championship.

Although their original partnership failed to meet expectations, Howard 's latest comments suggest that the public perception of his relationship with Bryant never reflected the complete story.

articles.title: Is Wemby trying to impress? Victor Wembanyama jokingly admits that he “had to show off” with Selena Gomez in the stands
articles.standfirst: The 22-year-old produced another extraordinary NBA performance
articles.summary: The 22-year-old produced another extraordinary NBA performance
articles.body:
A sold-out crowd at Frost Bank Center witnessed another remarkable performance from Victor Wembanyama on Saturday night, but the San Antonio Spurs star admitted that one particular spectator had given him an extra reason to put on a show.

Selena Gomez was sitting courtside as Wembanyama produced one of the most extraordinary statistical performances of his young NBA career, leading San Antonio to a commanding 114-91 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans .

The 22-year-old Frenchman finished with 50 points, 18 rebounds, five blocks and four steals in just 32 minutes, reinforcing his reputation as one of the league's most dominant players.

However, it was his reaction to a successful three-pointer that generated an unexpected talking point after the game.

Wembanyama appeared to glance toward the crowd following the shot, prompting a reporter to ask whether he had been acknowledging someone in attendance.

"Of course I had to show off for Selena, you know," Wembanyama replied with a smile, drawing laughter from reporters.

His lighthearted admission provided a memorable conclusion to an evening that had already established another significant milestone in his rapidly developing career.

Victor Wembanyama makes NBA history with Selena Gomez watching courtside

Wembanyama's performance was remarkable from the opening half, when he accumulated 32 points, 13 rebounds, three blocks and three steals to help San Antonio establish a 61-45 advantage.

The Spurs center eventually converted 20 of his 29 field-goal attempts, including five three-pointers, while making five of six free throws.

His combination of scoring, rebounding and defensive contributions made him the first player in NBA history to record at least 50 points, 18 rebounds, five blocks, four steals and five three-pointers in a single game.

New Orleans attempted to disrupt his rhythm through physical defense, with several confrontations resulting in technical fouls during the opening half.

Wembanyama remained largely unaffected, responding with another impressive scoring sequence that included a powerful one-handed dunk against Yves Missi .

The victory improved San Antonio's record to 14-3, keeping the Spurs level with the Los Angeles Lakers near the top of the Western Conference standings.

Spurs superstar explains his unusual comments about stat padding

Beyond his exchange about Gomez , Wembanyama attracted attention with another playful remark concerning the pursuit of individual scoring milestones.

"It is very special. Unlike many of my peers, I'm not very good at stat padding," he said during his on-court interview.

The Frenchman subsequently clarified his comments, explaining that he looks toward established NBA stars when deciding how aggressively to pursue scoring opportunities.

"But the greats, they don't think about that. I don't think LeBron, Shai, Jokic, Doncic think about that. And I have them as examples. So I try not to think about it either," he explained.

Wembanyama also revealed that coach Mitch Johnson had given him a final opportunity to reach 50 points before withdrawing him from the game.

"(Johnson) did tell me that at some point I had 1:30 left of play time and he said he wished I had come to 50, but I only have 1:30 left and I told him it might be enough," Wembanyama recalled.

The achievement marked his second 50-point performance of November, with Stephon Castle contributing another 19 points and six assists in the victory.

While the numbers demonstrated Wembanyama's growing influence on the court, his joking acknowledgment of Gomez revealed a more relaxed side to the young superstar following another historic performance.

The Frenchman subsequently clarified his comments, explaining that he looks toward established NBA stars when deciding how aggressively to pursue scoring opportunities.
"But the greats, they don't think about that. I don't think LeBron, Shai, Jokic, Doncic think about that. And I have them as examples. So I try not to think about it either," he explained.
Wembanyama also revealed that coach Mitch Johnson had given him a final opportunity to reach 50 points before withdrawing him from the game.
"(Johnson) did tell me that at some point I had 1:30 left of play time and he said he wished I had come to 50, but I only have 1:30 left and I told him it might be enough," Wembanyama recalled.
The achievement marked his second 50-point performance of November, with Stephon Castle contributing another 19 points and six assists in the victory.

While the numbers demonstrated Wembanyama's growing influence on the court, his joking acknowledgment of Gomez revealed a more relaxed side to the young superstar following another historic performance.

articles.title: LeBron James has a special message from his “nephew” for the Bucks point guard who grew up playing with Bryce James
articles.standfirst: After rookie guard Brayden Burries erupted for a career-high 26 points off the bench in Philadelphia, the 76ers superstar celebrated a full-circle moment with a former Strive for Greatness standout he has mentored since childhood
articles.summary: After rookie guard Brayden Burries erupted for a career-high 26 points off the bench in Philadelphia, the 76ers superstar celebrated a full-circle moment with a former Strive for Greatness standout he has mentored since childhood
articles.body:
Over more than two decades in the NBA , LeBron James has shared the hardwood with the sons of former rivals, squared off against players raised idolizing him, and prepared for matchups against his own eldest son, Bronny James .

On Saturday afternoon in Philadelphia, however, the new Philadelphia 76ers forward experienced a deeply personal milestone of a different kind, facing off against Brayden Burries , a 21-year-old Milwaukee Bucks rookie whom James has coached, mentored, and treated like family for more than a decade.

Inside Xfinity Mobile Arena, Eastern Conference-leading Philadelphia (14-3) narrowly survived a furious fourth-quarter push from Milwaukee (1-16) to claim a 132-129 victory.

Bucks guard Tyler Herro commanded plenty of headlines with a career-high 50-point explosion, and nearly forced overtime before officials ruled his final right-wing three-pointer left his fingertips just after the buzzer, prompting 76ers center Joel Embiid to reportedly praise Herro as a “top-five player in the league.”

Yet amid the late-game drama, James’s focus quickly turned to Burries, who poured in a career-best 26 points, including a clutch corner three with 4.8 seconds left that briefly pulled Milwaukee within a single point.

Shortly after the final horn, the official NBA social media account captured the postgame embrace between veteran and rookie, posting: “@braydenburries0 embraced his former AAU coach, @kingjames, after they faced each other today in Philly! 🙌.”

James soon reposted the clip to his Instagram Story with an emotional tribute to the young guard he affectionately calls family: “So proud of him!! so so so proud! Keep going nephew 🙏🏻🫡🫶.”

From youth AAU courts and Arizona to facing off on an NBA floor

The bond between James and Burries stretches back long before either imagined sharing an NBA court.

Burries first connected with the James family when he was roughly eight years old, eventually rising through the ranks on the Nike EYBL circuit with James’s Strive for Greatness AAU program. Playing alongside LeBron’s youngest son, Bryce James , Burries developed into a premier prospect before carrying that friendship to the college level at the University of Arizona.

In fact, Bryce played a direct role in steering Burries toward Tucson as part of the Wildcats’ highly touted recruiting class. Recalling how his longtime teammate recruited him to join the program, Burries explained that Bryce reached out with a simple pitch: “Yo, come to Arizona.”

The two remained close throughout their time together with the Wildcats, and when Milwaukee selected Burries with the 10th overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Bryce celebrated the milestone on Instagram by posting “Prada u boy” accompanied by four red hearts.

Entering the league with lottery-pick expectations, Burries has provided a bright spot during an otherwise difficult opening month for the Bucks. Across his first 16 appearances prior to Saturday’s matinee, he averaged 10.4 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 2.3 assists.

Even after shifting back to a reserve role against Philadelphia following a 10-game stretch as a starter, the rookie showcased the poise, rebounding, and scoring punch that boosted his 17-game season averages to approximately 11.3 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 2.4 assists per contest, guided by a foundational piece of advice James gave him years ago: “Just be you, go out there and compete, have fun, play hard.”

Of course, the 22-time All-Star made sure his former pupil did not leave Philadelphia with a victory. James stuffed the box score with 21 points, six rebounds, six assists, and three steals on 9-of-14 shooting in 35 minutes of action.

He sparked a 38-33 third-quarter turnaround by throwing down an emphatic dunk, rejecting a Kyle Kuzma shot, and feeding Tyrese Maxey for a go-ahead basket, before pouring in 13 of his 21 points during the fourth quarter to seal the win for Philadelphia, turning a hard-fought Eastern Conference battle into an unforgettable afternoon for mentor and protégé alike.

articles.title: The giant Walker Kessler who is as crucial for the Lakers as Doncic: "It may sound like blasphemy..."
articles.standfirst: Center Walker Kessler is having a major impact on the Lakers' strong performance, led by Luka Doncic, at the start of the season
articles.summary: Center Walker Kessler is having a major impact on the Lakers' strong performance, led by Luka Doncic, at the start of the season
articles.body:
At Sports Illustrated they believe that Walker Kessler , the giant engaged to Miss America , is as important as Luka Doncic to the Lakers .

Chris Mannix and Evan Turner analyze the impact of the giant Walker Kessler (2.18 m and 111 kg) on the Los Angeles Lakers' game, especially his incredible defensive performance and the balance he creates on offense (he has a special connection with Doncic when running "pick-and-rolls" (screen-and-rolls)).

It is possible to win an NBA championship with a middling defense, so the reality is that they depend as much on Kessler on defense as they do on Doncic on offense

"It may sound like blasphemy, but who do they have who is capable of taking on Kessler’s role: grabbing rebounds, blocking shots, and cleaning things up on defense?" they ask.

Chris Mannix and Evan Turner believe that the Lakers "have a fairly narrow margin for error" and that "it is possible to win an NBA championship with an average-level defense, as Denver showed three or four years ago, so the reality is that they depend as much on Kessler on defense as on Doncic on offense".

For the Lakers to succeed, they need Kessler to play, more or less, around 70 games... He is one of the 15 best defensive players in the NBA and a fundamental piece of the system

"For the Lakers to succeed, they need Kessler, who missed most of the 2025-26 season because of a shoulder injury, to play roughly around 70 games... He is one of the 15 best defensive players in the NBA and a fundamental piece of the system," they concluded about the center, who arrived in Los Angeles from the Utah Jazz in exchange for two future first-round Draft picks and two future first-round pick swap rights.

Rob Pelinka already warned it: "At the core of every great Lakers team there is a dominant big man"

Rob Pelinka, president of basketball operations and general manager of the Los Angeles Lakers, already warned after signing Kessler that "at the core of every great Lakers team there is a dominant big man."

Since his NBA debut in the 2022-23 season, only Victor Wembanyama has averaged more blocks per game than Kessler.

The statistics confirm Walker Kessler's impact on Doncic's Lakers

Walker Kessler, who signed with the Lakers for $130 million over four years , is averaging 14.3 points (he leads the NBA with a 66.4% field-goal percentage), 10.7 rebounds, and 2.1 blocks in 30.9 minutes.

With Kessler on the court, the Lakers allow only 111.0 points per 100 possessions and reduce opponents' shooting accuracy near the rim by nearly 13%. Advanced metrics from "Cleaning the Glass" highlight that the center has the third-best On/Off differential on the entire roster (+7.3 Plus/Minus per game), behind only Doncic and Austin Reaves.

One of his weak points is his accuracy from the free-throw line, where he makes only 59.7% of his shots.
